app_fee.value: International applicants apply for free for each degree application.
app_fee.quote: International applicants can now apply for free for each degree or licensure application.

fee_waiver.value: Because international applicants apply free, they do not need a separate waiver.
fee_waiver.quote: International applicants can now apply for free for each degree or licensure application.

gre_general.value: The graduate pages set no university-wide GRE rule; each program states its own.

toefl_min.value: A TOEFL score of 4.0 on the new scale (79 on the old) is the minimum for applicants without a U.S. degree.

ielts_min.value: An IELTS band of 6 or higher is the minimum for applicants without a U.S. degree.
ielts_min.quote: A band 6 or higher through the International English Language Testing System (IELTS)

english_waiver.value: India is not on the university's list of English-official countries, so Indian applicants need a test score unless they hold a U.S. degree.
english_waiver.quote: If your native language is not English and you do not have a degree from a regionally accredited U.S. college or university, you must have a minimum score on one of the following exams

also.quote: If you have graduated from a school in a country where English is the official language for higher education, you will not be required to demonstrate English proficiency.
The international admissions team will accept Duolingo English test scores of 110 or higher as an alternative

notes: Fee sources conflict. The international admissions home page (current) says international applicants apply free; the graduate application checklist still says $70 and the MBA page says $70 for internationals; the graduate admission page says $40 per degree application. The international page is used. The General Requirements policy 5020 PDF is out of date and was not used. Deadlines are set per program; the university's international preferred Fall date is June 30. The English-official country list (https://www.wright.edu/international-education/international-students/english-as-official-language) does not include India. Program-level exceptions were fetched for Engineering, Biomedical Sciences, Environmental Sciences and Electrical Engineering.
